description: Review a migration's current discovery findings and return the open risks, highest severity first, each with a next step: who to ask and what to ask. Call after each discovery iteration with the full, cumulative findings (open questions with answer null) and the same engagement_id, to see which risks are new, still open or closed. Minimal example submission: {"engagement_id": "acme-crm-2026", "sow": {"use_case": "Consolidate two legacy CRMs into one Salesforce org.", "scope": ["Account", "Contact", "Opportunity"]}, "project_items": [{"category": "purpose", "question": "Why choose to migrate now?", "answer": "Legacy CRM contract ends in Q2.", "source": {"who": "VP Sales"}}], "objects": [{"name": "Account", "criticality": "high", "has_hierarchy": true, "items": [{"category": "object_context", "question": "What does Account mean to the business?", "answer": null}], "flags": [{"description": "Parent hierarchy source not provided", "owner": "Finance"}]}]}

DiscoveredOutsideScope.description:
Optional. An object or table Discovery found that isn't in scope. If it isn't clear whether
something is in scope, ask the scope owner.

requested_by.description: Role of whoever asked for it.
requested_by.title: Requested By

timing.description: Day 1 or a planned fast follow.

DiscoveredOutsideScope.title: DiscoveredOutsideScope

sow.description: Scope baseline, if you have it. Without it, in-scope checks are skipped; scope is reviewed from your scope answers.

waiting_on.description: What the object is waiting on.
waiting_on.title: Waiting On

ObjectCategory.description:
Object- or table-level topic. object_context: what it means to the business, who owns and
uses it, record types and Day 1 needs. object_source: where its data comes from, static files,
record counts and keys. dependencies: what must exist before it can load and reference data
still changing. hierarchy: its source and target hierarchy, if it has one. migration_logic:
which records move, how far back, logic by business unit, and whether original dates and owners
are kept.
ObjectCategory.title: ObjectCategory

name.description: Object or table name, e.g. Account.
name.title: Name

ProjectCategory.description:
Project-level topic. purpose: why the migration is happening and the pain points behind
it. scope: what data is in scope, Day 1 vs fast follow, and when scope freezes. use_case: what
the migration should accomplish and the priority of each use case. success: what Day 1
readiness looks like and who validates and signs off on the migrated data. people: business
units and users, decision makers and the scope owner. data_landscape: where the data lives and
its condition, other loads, integrations, compliance data, harmonization and governance.
procurement: what the client has purchased (context only, not scored; only if known).
process: how each business unit uses the system today, its processes and key reports.
ProjectCategory.title: ProjectCategory

question.description: The question as the agent asked it.
question.title: Question

SOW.description: The scope baseline, e.g. from the statement of work. Optional: leave it out if you don't have it.
SOW.title: SOW

who.description: Role of the person who gave the answer, e.g. 'VP Sales'. Use a role, not a name.
who.title: Who

name: validate_migration_discovery

closed.description: Risk IDs from last time that are now resolved.
closed.title: Closed

new.description: Risk IDs that weren't there last time.
new.title: New

not_resubmitted.description: Risk IDs from last time whose question, flag or object was left out of this submission. They are not resolved: send the full, current findings each time.
not_resubmitted.title: Not Resubmitted

id.description: Stable across submissions for the same engagement.
id.title: Id

must_confirm.description: Consent, compliance or legal topic, or a rule that could change data in ways that are hard to undo: stays open until confirmed.
must_confirm.title: Must Confirm

next_step.description: What to ask, and of whom.
next_step.title: Next Step

outputSchema.description: Surfaces risks. Never a pass/fail verdict, never a score.

changes.description: Change since the last submission; needs engagement_id.

risks_omitted.description: Lower-severity risks left out by max_risks or the no-key limit.
risks_omitted.title: Risks Omitted
